newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.N. organises EU maize shipment to North Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.N. organises EU maize shipment to North Korea.

text.p: Grain traders said on Wednesday they had been asked to supply 24,000 tonnes of European Union maize for distribution as food aid in famine-struck North Korea.
The shipments to North Korea, whose maize crop has been devastated by a severe drought in recent weeks, are being organised by the United Nations' World Food Programme in Rome.
Traders said they were offering to sell the grain in a tender which asked for maize to be packed in bags and shipped by October 19. The grain was likely to be supplied from France.
"We expect to have the results of the tender on Friday," a trader said.
Famine in North Korea has worsened sharply and people in the Stalinist state are now openly talking about starving children dying, international aid agencies there said on Wednesday.
In a joint forum pleading for donations and help, the agencies said the troubled nation would need at least 700,000 tonnes of grain to tide it through to October.

The World Food Programme said last month it had approved shipments of 130,000 tonnes of commodities worth $45.7 million to feed children in nurseries and kindergartens. That would bring the total amount pledged by the WFP to $141.5 million.

The agency said donors who had agreed to supply the badly needed food included the United States, European Union, Ireland, Norway, the OPEC oil producers' cartel and Archer Daniels Midland Co, a private U.S. grains firm.
The WFP said domestic stocks were almost depleted and it was essential new food arrived before the October harvest.
North Korea's famine began in 1995 when severe floods destroyed arable land, crops, fertiliser stores and irrigation systems, plunging the country into a dire food shortage.
The recent drought of over 60 days destroyed some 1.5 million tonnes of maize which the country had expected would help cover its needs between November 1997 and October 1998.
Officials estimate that 37.6 percent, or 800,000, of children aged up to six years old are suffering from malnutrition. Of these, 80,000 suffer severe malnutrition.
